description: GE HealthCare Technologies Inc. engages in the development, manufacture, and marketing of products, services, and complementary digital solutions used in the diagnosis, treatment, and monitoring of patients in the United States, Canada, and internationally. Craig explained how the trust’s actively managed strategy targets companies with characteristics attractive to major pharmaceutical groups. Insmed was its largest portfolio holding ahead of the deal, with Sanofi’s US$175-per-share offer representing a 46% premium to the pre-announcement share price and potentially boosting the trust’s net asset value (NAV). She also discussed the sustainability of the trust’s dividend, explaining how acquisition proceeds support its capital-funded dividend policy. Craig said the M&A wave was gathering pace, with ten portfolio companies involved in deals this year, against nine last year and a historical annual average of four to five. She identified the pharmaceutical industry's approaching patent cliff, with around US$400 billion in drug sales facing patent expirations, as a major catalyst. More than 70% of new drugs last year originated in biotechnology, underlining the sector’s growing importance to pharmaceutical innovation. headlines.title: Palantir Rips 10% to Lead Software Stocks. Cloudflare and ServiceNow Also Join ‘Jensen Rally’
headlines.summary: Eric Bleeker, Chief Investment Officer at 24/7 Wall St., says Jensen Huang's return to NVIDIA is lifting technology stocks on Monday. The NASDAQ was up more than 7% as of 1:30 p.m. Eastern, after opening with a 3% pre-market gain following Friday's sell-off. Chip stocks as a group rose more than 13%. Software is also higher, but the gains are uneven. Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT) and Salesforce (NYSE: CRM) are each up about 3%, while the IGV software ETF is up 4%. The biggest winners are companies that benefit from sovereign AI and a strong open-weight ecosystem. Palantir (NASDAQ: PLTR) leads at 10%, and Palantir has been one of the loudest backers of sovereign AI. Cloudflare (NYSE: NET) is up roughly 7%, and ServiceNow (NYSE: NOW) is up 5%, helped by its control tower software that guides customers between models and agentic workloads. Anthropic is lagging, since Huang has pushed open-weight models that pressure leading labs like Anthropic and OpenAI. Bleeker's takeaway: if Huang keeps backing open weight model makers, Palantir, Cloudflare and ServiceNow, up 5% to 10%, should keep outperforming the 2% to 3% gains in the rest of software.
